title: Getting started
keywords: start beginning scenario problem open new solve example
body:
A scenario contains nodes, networks and any number of problems. At the top left you choose the problem you are editing and solving.

- **Open** loads an .llab file, **New** starts an empty scenario. The ⋯ menu offers an **example** and the **import** of old LogisticsLab files.
- In the **Nodes** tab you create the places and give them their role in the problem, in the **Network** tab the edges, in the **Parameters** tab the settings of the problem.
- **Solve** (⌘↩) computes the problem. The result appears in the **Solution** tab and on the map.

Before solving, the app checks that all necessary data is there and names missing values together with the node.

title: Creating and editing nodes
keywords: node place location create delete address coordinates map click active inactive geocoding
body:
- **On the map:** choose the “Add nodes” icon at the top left. Every click into the map then adds a node until ✕ ends the mode. The address is fetched automatically where possible.
- **In the list:** “+ Node” creates a node, the next click into the map sets its position.
- **From an address to coordinates:** enter the address and choose “Look up coordinates”.
- The list only shows the nodes, you edit them in the form below. ↑ and ↓ change the node, Enter moves to the next field of the form.
- Inactive nodes stay in the scenario but are left out of every problem.
- The **ID** is given automatically. It is only a key for edges, files and imports, so it is not in the list but in the form beside the name; it can be changed there, for example to match Excel.

title: Roles
keywords: role supplier customer transshipment candidate depot filter other
body:
The role says what a node is in the current problem, for example supplier or customer in a transportation problem.

- A node has exactly one role per problem. A second click on the chip removes it.
- Roles for other problems of the scenario (for example depot) are kept, “All roles” shows them.
- The filters above the list show the nodes of one role. Transshipment nodes are nodes of the network without a role in the problem.
- A new node gets the role of the selected filter.

title: Networks and edges
keywords: network edge edges draw connections direction directed undirected capacity fixed costs
body:
Network flows, the shortest path and the Chinese postman need a network, for the transportation problem and the TSP it is optional. In the **Network** tab you choose the network of the problem or create a new one.

- **Draw edge:** click the start node and then the end node on the map.
- **Create all connections:** for transportation problems from the suppliers (via the transshipment nodes) to the customers, for the TSP, the shortest path and the Chinese postman all nodes with each other.
- **Direction:** in transportation problems the edges lead from the suppliers to the customers, edges drawn the wrong way round are turned. For the TSP, the shortest path and the Chinese postman each edge is directed or undirected.
- Values of the edges such as capacity or fixed costs are in the form. Some only take effect once the matching parameter is switched on.

title: Transportation problem (TPP)
keywords: transportation problem tpp objective costs contribution quantity bottleneck ranges capacity fixed costs single source block cost rate
body:
Suppliers deliver directly to customers. You choose the objective in the Parameters tab:

- **Minimise costs:** the usual variant.
- **Maximise contribution:** revenue per unit at the customer minus cost per unit at the supplier minus transport costs.
- **Maximise quantity:** the largest quantity delivered, supply and demand are upper bounds.
- **Minimise bottleneck:** the largest cost rate of the connections used becomes as small as possible.

Optional are ranges for supply and demand, capacities and fixed costs of the connections (via a network), single sourcing and blocking connections by the smallest or largest cost rate. The supply may be smaller than the demand.

title: Location problems (DLP)
keywords: location locations dlp wlp warehouse p-median p-centre set covering maximal covering mcp scp candidates radius budget coverage
body:
Locations are opened among candidates, every customer is assigned to an open location.

- **Warehouse location (WLP):** operating costs of the candidates plus transport costs as low as possible; optionally with capacities.
- **p-median:** exactly p locations, the sum of the distances (optionally weighted by demand) as low as possible.
- **p-centre:** exactly p locations, the longest distance to a customer as short as possible.
- **Set covering:** every customer within the radius of an open location – as few locations or the lowest operating costs.
- **Maximal covering:** cover as much demand as possible within the radius for a budget (operating costs or number of locations).

- **Nodes:** candidates with operating costs and capacity, customers with demand – empty counts as 1.
- **Measure:** for the WLP as for the transportation problem, otherwise distances by default. The radius is in the unit of the measure.
- **Map:** for set and maximal covering, circles show the radius around the candidates, with a solution around the open locations. On roads the radius is a distance along them; the circle shows it as the crow flies.
- **Solution:** the locations with customers, quantity, utilisation and operating costs, and the assignment of the customers. For maximal covering the customers not covered are listed below.

If in set covering a customer is outside the radius of every candidate, or p is larger than the number of candidates, the app reports this before solving.

title: Network flows
keywords: network flow min cost flow max flow maximum flow source sink multicommodity commodities multimodal modes warehouses multi-stage balance shortages
body:
Quantities flow over the edges of a network.

- **Min cost flow:** from supply to demand at minimal cost. Edges have capacities and minimum flows, nodes a throughput.
- **Max flow:** the largest quantity from a source to a sink – or from all suppliers to all customers, then supply and demand are the limits.
- **Multicommodity:** several commodities share the capacities. You create the commodities in the Parameters tab.
- **Multimodal:** the allowed modes of transport per edge, each with its own costs and capacities.
- **Multi-stage warehouses:** open warehouses (candidates) in the network and distribute the quantities through them.

The balance “automatic” allows shortages, “exact” requires supply and demand to be equal.

title: Round trip and passage (TSP)
keywords: tsp round trip passage tour start end open end open start shortest paths auxiliary nodes
body:
The shortest tour through all active nodes. The kind of tour can be a round trip (back to the start), a passage (from the start to the end), an open end, an open start or completely open.

Without a network the distances of the matrix apply. With a network the tour follows the shortest paths in the network – auxiliary nodes such as junctions and directed edges block or allow ways. If there is no possible tour, the app names the section without a way.

title: Shortest path
keywords: shortest path route start end network dijkstra
body: The shortest path from a start to an end in the network, valued by distance, time or costs. Edges can be directed one by one. If no path reaches the end, the app says so. The solution shows the sections with their length and the total so far.

title: Chinese postman (CPP)
keywords: chinese postman cpp edge edges traverse street cleaning winter service refuse collection round
body:
The shortest tour that traverses every edge of the network at least once from the start and returns to it – typical for street cleaning, winter service or refuse collection.

- The network is required. Each edge can be directed (one-way street) or undirected.
- Edges that cannot be reached otherwise are traversed more than once. The solution shows the length of all edges, the extra distance and how often edges are traversed again.
- If no way leads from a node back to the start, the app says so before solving.

title: Vehicle routing (VRP)
keywords: vehicle routing vrp vehicle vehicles depot customers capacity time window service time maximum time distance tours
body:
The vehicles drive from the depot to the customers and back. The aim is tours with the shortest total distance.

- **Nodes:** exactly one node with the role depot with its operating time (start of the tours, latest return), the customers with demand, service time and – if switched on – a time window. Times are entered as times of the day, e.g. 08:30.
- **Vehicles** are created in the Parameters tab: capacity and number of identical vehicles. If the number is left empty, the app uses as few tours as possible and only then the shortest distance.
- **Options:** observe time windows, start all tours at the start time of the depot (otherwise each tour leaves as late as possible so that it does not wait), maximum time and maximum distance per tour.
- **Solution:** each tour in its own colour – where tours use the same road, their lines lie side by side. A click on a tour of the overview highlights it on the map, a click on a section only that section. The overview shows per tour and in total stops, quantity, utilisation, distance, total time as well as start and return; below, per tour, the sections with departure, driving time, waiting, arrival (after the waiting, i.e. the start of the service), the time window for comparison, service, quantity and distance. The node list shows the time windows in a column of their own; hovering over a node shows demand, service time and time window.

If the demand of a customer fits into no vehicle, the app says so before solving.

title: Pickup and delivery / dial-a-ride (PDP, DARP)
keywords: pickup delivery pdp darp dial-a-ride fahrgast passenger pick up deliver amount load vehicles depot capacity time windows tours
body:
Every quantity is picked up at its pickup and brought to its delivery node – on the same tour, the pickup before the delivery. The load of the vehicle never exceeds its capacity. The tours with the shortest total distance are searched.

- **Nodes:** exactly one depot with its operating time, the pickups with amount and delivery node, the delivery nodes with their delivered amount – the sum of the amounts brought there, shown only. You choose the delivery node in the form of the pickup among the nodes with the role delivery; several pickups may share a delivery node. Pickups have a service time. At a delivery node the service consists of a stop time per stop (stopping, parking, walking to the door) and a time per unit delivered; several quantities brought to the same delivery node one after another make one stop with one stop time. Time windows – if switched on – apply to both.
- **Map:** a dashed line connects every pickup with its delivery node.
- **Vehicles, times and options** as in vehicle routing (VRP).
- **Dial-a-ride (DARP):** when people are carried, the longest ride per passenger and the largest detour factor (e.g. 2 = at most twice the direct ride) limit the time in the vehicle – with both the stricter applies. Without a limit it is a PDP.
- **Solution:** per section the quantity with its sign (+ picked up, − delivered) and the load afterwards. The table **Rides** shows per pickup the tour, quantity, direct ride, ride in the vehicle and the detour. In the overview the quantity is the amount picked up; the utilisation refers to the highest load of the tour.

If a pickup has no delivery node or it is not a delivery, the app reports this before solving.

title: Reading the solution
keywords: solution result objective key figure connections utilisation commodity mode stale llsol save
body:
- The key figure of the objective has a blue frame.
- The table shows the connections with quantity, cost rate, costs and utilisation, for tours the sections with length and “so far”. A click highlights the connection on the map in orange.
- For multicommodity and multimodal problems “Commodity:” or “Mode:” shows a single one.
- The node list shows target, actual, share or utilisation and the partners. Filters find, for example, unmet demand or fully used nodes.
- When the data changes, the solution is marked as out of date. “Save as .llsol” stores the solution.
- The icon beside “Solution” switches on the **wide view**: the data area becomes wide, the map narrow – for large solutions such as vehicle routing. A second click restores the width. Wide tables scroll sideways.

A click on a supplier or location – on the map or in the table of the locations – highlights all its connections; a click on a single connection removes it again.

title: Map
keywords: map layers legend colours centre zoom labels hover
body:
- Top left: add nodes and draw edges. Top right: layers (network, solution, labels). Bottom right: centre the problem and zoom.
- Colours: suppliers blue, customers green, candidates violet, transshipment nodes grey diamonds. Used edges are blue, unused ones petrol, the selected connection orange.
- The mouse pointer over an edge or a node shows its values. Labels that would overlap are hidden.

The symbols are the same in all problems: square – source or start (supplier, depot, pickup, start), ring – destination or demand (customer, delivery, stops, end), diamond – location (candidate, filled if open), grey dot – transit (transshipment node, other nodes of the network).

title: Distances and costs
keywords: matrix distance time costs osm road network straight line cost per km cost per hour valuation
body:
In the Parameters tab under **Matrix** you choose the road network (OSM) or straight lines and enter the cost per km and per hour. The matrix applies to all problems of the scenario.

The **valuation** of a problem (distances, travel times, costs) decides what is optimised. “Costs” needs a cost per km or per hour.

title: Files and import
keywords: file llab llsol save open import logisticslab 5 tppx clpx dlpx nwfx tspx vrpx quit
body:
- **.llab** is the scenario, **.llsol** a saved solution.
- **Import:** files of LogisticsLab 5 (TPPX, CLPX, DLPX, NWFX, TSPX, VRPX) are converted. Files of LogisticsLab 4 are not supported.
- When you quit with unsaved changes, the app asks whether to save them.

title: Computing: local or server
keywords: compute local server settings internet cancel solver
body:
In the settings (gear icon) you choose whether to compute locally with the bundled solver or on a LogisticsLab server.

Road distances, routes and the address search use the servers of TH Wildau and OpenStreetMap services and need an internet connection. A running solve can be cancelled.

title: Keyboard
keywords: keyboard keys shortcut arrow keys enter
body:
- ⌘O open, ⌘S save, ⌘↩ solve, ⌘? or F1 help.
- ↑ and ↓ change the entry in the node, edge and solution lists.
- Enter completes an input and moves to the next field.

On Windows and Linux use Ctrl instead of ⌘.
